definitions.explanation: Overwhelming, destructive power, especially of natural disasters, epidemics, or other forces beyond human control. Almost always used with を振るう (to rage, to wreak havoc).

examples.japanese: ⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るった→振るう：12793_furuu⟧。
examples.english: The typhoon raged with devastating force.

examples.japanese: ⟦インフルエンザ→インフルエンザ：05384_infuruenza⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るっている→振るう：12793_furuu⟧。
examples.english: Influenza is raging across the entire country.

examples.japanese: ⟦{記録的|きろくてき}→記録的：28788_kirokuteki⟧な⟦{大雪|おおゆき}→大雪：03017_ooyuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るい→振るう：12793_furuu⟧、⟦{交通機関|こうつうきかん}→交通機関：21264_koutsuukikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{完全|かんぜん}→完全：01552_kanzen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ストップ⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Record-breaking heavy snow raged and public transportation came to a complete halt.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the fixed phrase {猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るう→振るう：12793_furuu⟧ (to rage, to wreak havoc). Rarely appears outside this collocation. Subjects are typically natural disasters (⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧, ⟦{地震|じしん}→地震：01608_jishin⟧), diseases (⟦インフルエンザ→インフルエンザ：05384_infuruenza⟧, ⟦ウイルス→ウイルス：05223_uirusu⟧), or other destructive forces.
This word is a bound noun — it almost never appears alone without ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るう→振るう：12793_furuu⟧. Learning the full phrase is more useful than learning the word in isolation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るう→振るう：12793_furuu⟧ (to rage, to wreak havoc)
- {猛威|もうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ふるい⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧ (to continue raging)
- ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{猛威|もうい} (the fury of nature)
